advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish 'both sub-writes failed' (empty buffer) from 'nothing to write' before returning success from _write_success_finalize, so a fully-failed finalize is not counted as processed.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:469-474 `with _seam.batch_sink(buffered): ds.emit(...) ; _queue.mark_done(...)` then `if not buffered: return`
digest_sidecar.emit swallows all exceptions and returns False without appending: src/rebar/llm/overlap/digest_sidecar.py:112-114 `except Exception: logger.warning(...); return False`
queue._append swallows all exceptions and returns False without appending: src/rebar/llm/overlap/queue.py:88-90 `except Exception: logger.warning(...); return False`
caller counts it as success regardless: src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:529-530 `_write_success_finalize(...)` then `processed += 1`
advisory.finding: `if not buffered: return` treats a completely-failed finalize as success. Both `ds.emit` and `_queue.mark_done` are best-effort (they swallow their own exceptions and append nothing to the buffer on failure). If BOTH fail inside the `batch_sink`, `buffered` is empty, the function returns early as though it succeeded, the fallback never fires, and the caller unconditionally does `processed += 1`. A finalize that wrote NOTHING is indistinguishable from one that wrote both events.
scenarios: Store read/write hiccup or secret-screen refusal makes both emits no-op; drain reports processed but the ticket is neither digested nor marked done, and it stays enqueued/re-claimable forever without any error signal.
advisory.suggested_fix: Have ds.emit/mark_done report success back (they already return bool), and only treat an empty buffer as success when both returned True; otherwise log/fallback.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard against committing a DONE_ENRICH-only (digest-missing) batch: require both the digest and DONE to be buffered before batch_write_and_push, else fall back or re-enqueue.
evidence: Buffer is populated by whichever of the two best-effort calls succeeds: src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:470-471
emit failure is silent (no exception, no buffer entry): src/rebar/llm/overlap/digest_sidecar.py:112-114
fallback only fires on batch_write_and_push raising: src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:476-485 `try: batch_write_and_push(...) except Exception:`
DONE tombstone marks the ticket done: src/rebar/llm/overlap/queue.py:108-110 `mark_done ... append DONE_ENRICH (completion tombstone)`
advisory.finding: A partially-populated buffer commits a DONE_ENRICH tombstone WITHOUT a TICKET_DIGEST, and the fallback never repairs it. If `ds.emit` fails (silently, returning False) but `_queue.mark_done` succeeds inside the `batch_sink`, the buffer contains only the DONE_ENRICH event; `if not buffered: return` does not catch this (buffer is non-empty), `batch_write_and_push` succeeds committing DONE-only, and the fallback is skipped because no exception was raised — leaving the ticket permanently marked done with no digest.
scenarios: Digest emit blocked (secret-screen refusal / transient read fault) while the DONE append succeeds: ticket is tombstoned as enriched but has no digest and will not be re-enqueued.
advisory.suggested_fix: Check the emit result: if ds.emit returned False, do not proceed to commit a DONE-only batch — skip the mark_done and re-enqueue (matching the stale-skip posture), or fall back to sequential and surface the failure.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that makes event_append.batch_write_and_push raise during a successful drain and asserts the ticket still reaches present-fresh + done (fallback sequential writes ran).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:476-485: `try: event_append.batch_write_and_push(tracker, buffered) except Exception: logger.warning(...); ds.emit(...); _queue.mark_done(...)`
search of tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py for 'batch_write_and_push' returns (no matches) and for 'fallback' returns only an unrelated comment — no test monkeypatches batch_write_and_push to raise

Named violating input: monkeypatch.setattr(event_append, 'batch_write_and_push', raise RuntimeError) then D.drain(...) — the sequential fallback lines execute only in this world and are currently unexercised, so a regression that drops the fallback (leaving the ticket unenriched and pending forever) would go undetected
advisory.finding: The newly added batch-failure fallback in _write_success_finalize (the except Exception branch that re-runs ds.emit + _queue.mark_done sequentially when batch_write_and_push raises) has no test — the fault is never injected at the batch seam, so the recovery contract 'a batched finalize that fails still writes the digest and DONE_ENRICH via sequential writes' is unverified.
scenarios: A transient batched commit/push failure during a successful finalize; the fallback must still land the digest and DONE tombstone
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test using monkeypatch.setattr(event_append, 'batch_write_and_push', raising side effect) around D.drain, then assert ds.freshness(tid)=='present-fresh' and Q.reduce_ticket(tid)['done'] is True, plus that a warning was logged.
